claim: Agent Skills are directories containing a SKILL.md file (with required YAML frontmatter: name and description) plus optional bundled scripts/resources, which agents discover and load dynamically to perform better at specific tasks.
stance_target: the SOP-to-Agent-Skills architecture (pillar 2) as a concrete, implementable packaging format for procedural knowledge
scope_conditions: Anthropic's Agent Skills standard, published Oct 2025, open cross-platform standard as of Dec 2025
quoted_support: A skill is a directory containing a SKILL.md file that contains organized folders of instructions, scripts, and resources that give agents additional capabilities.

claim: Progressive disclosure across three levels (frontmatter metadata pre-loaded at startup, full SKILL.md body loaded only if relevant, and bundled sub-files read only as needed) means the amount of context bundleable into a skill is effectively unbounded without consuming the active context window.
stance_target: scalable skill-sequence architecture for an autonomous software factory managing many specialized agent departments without context-window exhaustion
scope_conditions: Agent Skills design for agents with filesystem and code-execution tools
quoted_support: Agents with a filesystem and code execution tools don't need to read the entirety of a skill into their context window when working on a particular task. This means that the amount of context that can be bundled into a skill is effectively unbounded.

claim: Skills can bundle executable code that an agent runs as a deterministic tool (e.g. a Python script extracting PDF form fields) without loading the script or target document into context, because some operations are both cheaper and more reliable via code execution than via token generation.
stance_target: pillar 2's distinction between probabilistic LLM reasoning and deterministic code execution within a skill sequence
scope_conditions: Agent Skills code-execution capability, worked PDF-skill example
quoted_support: For example, sorting a list via token generation is far more expensive than simply running a sorting algorithm. Beyond efficiency concerns, many applications require the deterministic reliability that only code can provide... And because code is deterministic, this workflow is consistent and repeatable.

claim: Skill development should start from evaluation -- running the agent on representative tasks to identify specific capability gaps, then building skills incrementally to address them, rather than authoring skills speculatively.
stance_target: rigid-evals-driven skill authoring workflow as the entry point to building an SOP library for a software factory's specialized agents
quoted_support: Start with evaluation: Identify specific gaps in your agents' capabilities by running them on representative tasks and observing where they struggle or require additional context. Then build skills incrementally to address these shortcomings.

claim: Malicious or untrusted skills can introduce environment vulnerabilities or direct an agent to exfiltrate data and take unintended actions; skills from less-trusted sources should be audited for bundled code dependencies, resources, and instructions directing connections to untrusted external network sources before use.
stance_target: installing and running third-party agent skills in a software factory without a security-audit gate
quoted_support: malicious skills may introduce vulnerabilities in the environment where they're used or direct Claude to exfiltrate data and take unintended actions. We recommend installing skills only from trusted sources. When installing a skill from a less-trusted source, thoroughly audit it before use.

claim: Anthropic's stated future direction for Skills includes enabling agents to create, edit, and evaluate their own Skills autonomously, letting agents codify their own behavioral patterns into reusable capabilities without human authoring.
stance_target: the long-term trajectory toward self-sustaining agentic loops that generate their own SOPs (pillar 2) without human-in-the-loop skill curation
scope_conditions: forward-looking statement, Anthropic roadmap as of Oct 2025
quoted_support: Looking further ahead, we hope to enable agents to create, edit, and evaluate Skills on their own, letting them codify their own patterns of behavior into reusable capabilities.
